message.content: When a skipper's chartplotter CSV and the boat's other receiver's NMEA dump both log the same trip, we flag a clash and the later import's voyage gets dropped from the hours. Operators hate it: it's one trip, not two. How do other logbook tools handle duplicate tracks from two devices? Get a scout to look, then tell me what we should do.

content.text: I'll look at what the dedupe does today, then send a scout to research the other tools.

input.prompt:
Research question, read-only, web plus this repo (tidewright, Go).

When two devices log the same trip (a chartplotter CSV export and an NMEA dump from another receiver), tidewright treats the overlapping voyages as a clash: see REQ-0108 and internal/voyage/dedupe.go. The user wants to know how other logbook and fleet-logging tools handle duplicate tracks of one trip from two devices.

Find: which tools merge, which pick one source, which flag; how each decides two tracks are the same trip; which source's engine hours count. Name each tool and link the page you read. Also note anything in the NMEA formats that tells devices apart, and what the Regulations in docs/regulation/ccvr-2021/text.md require of a voyage's track, if anything.

Facts with sources, no recommendation.
